questions.stem: A security team wants an Amazon EventBridge rule on the default event bus to start an investigation workflow whenever anyone calls read-only management APIs such as Describe* on sensitive resources. CloudTrail is enabled in the account. The rule is enabled, but it never matches these read-only calls, although it matches write calls. The team wants to fix this without writing code. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Move the rule to a partner event bus so that it receives all AWS management events.
Disable and enable the rule again so that EventBridge rebuilds its event pattern.
Create an AWS Lambda function that reads the CloudTrail log files in Amazon S3 and starts the workflow.

questions.stem: A company runs workloads in many AWS Regions in the standard partition. The operations team must be notified of account-specific AWS Health events from every Region, and of AWS Health events for AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), which are not Region-specific. The team wants as few Amazon EventBridge rules as possible. Which actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)

choices.text: Create one central rule in US West (Oregon) to receive account-specific AWS Health events from all standard partition Regions.
Create a rule in US East (N. Virginia) to receive global AWS Health events, such as events for IAM.
Create a rule in each Region where the workloads run, and rely on those rules to receive IAM events.
Use the simplified integration to also receive the public events that appear in the AWS Health Dashboard.
Create a rule only in the Region where the company's main workload runs; it receives events from all Regions.

questions.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations. The central operations team created an Amazon EventBridge rule for AWS Health events in its operations account, but the rule receives events only for the operations account. The team must receive AWS Health events for all accounts in the organization in one place, without deploying rules to every account. What should the team do with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.text: Keep the current rule, because EventBridge rules for AWS Health receive events for every account in the organization.
Use the AWS Health organizational view with delegated administrator access for the operations account to aggregate events from all accounts.
Deploy the same EventBridge rule to every member account with StackSets, and have each rule send email to the team.
Ask each account owner to check the AWS Health Dashboard every day and forward important events.

questions.stem: A web store account (111122223333) must send newOrderCreated events with the source com.exampleCorp.webStore to a central event bus named central-event-bus in a separate account (123456789012). The central account must accept only these events from the web store account, following least privilege. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST privilege?

choices.text: Attach a resource-based policy to the event bus in the web store account that allows account 123456789012 to read the events.
Attach a resource-based policy to central-event-bus in account 123456789012 that allows account 111122223333 to publish only events with that source and detail-type.
Attach a resource-based policy to central-event-bus that allows every account in the organization to publish any event.
Create an IAM user in account 123456789012 and store its access keys in the web store application to call PutEvents.
